CarPlay can significantly enhance the comfort and home-like feel of any car. However, the out-of-the-box experience isn't always perfect.

Some models still require a wired connection, and some don't support CarPlay at all, let alone provide iPhone charging and cooling on long journeys.

Fortunately, fixing these issues doesn't require a big investment. The affordable accessories below cover everything from wireless CarPlay and MagSafe charging to cable management and adding a full display to an older vehicle.

Upgrading wired CarPlay to wireless

If your car already supports wired CarPlay, the Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 lets you ditch the cable while retaining the vehicle's touchscreen, steering wheel controls, built-in microphone, and factory audio system.

This compact adapter features both USB-A and USB-C ports. After the initial pairing, it automatically reconnects every time you start the car. It also supports wireless Android Auto on Android 11 and above, making it especially handy for vehicles shared between iPhone and Android users.

One thing to note: this adapter requires the vehicle to come with wired CarPlay from the factory and cannot add CarPlay functionality to unsupported models.

The Carlinkit Mini Ultra 3 is available now for US$43.99, with free shipping for Prime members.

Adding CarPlay to nearly any older vehicle

If your car doesn't have CarPlay, buying a portable display is usually the simplest upgrade option. The Krunia 9.26-inch portable CarPlay display sells for US$89.99 and adds wireless CarPlay without removing the factory audio.

The display supports Bluetooth, AUX, and FM audio connections, and is compatible with Siri, Android Auto, and OTA firmware updates. It also comes with a reversing camera, though installing the camera requires running cabling to the rear of the car.

For drivers who want CarPlay but don't want to replace the head unit, this is a pretty attractive compromise.

Installing a permanent CarPlay head unit

A portable display may not suit every dashboard. For a neater permanent installation, the BOSS Audio BVCP9700A is a relatively affordable double-DIN head unit with a 7-inch touchscreen that supports Apple CarPlay, Android Auto, Bluetooth, and a reversing camera.

This head unit sells for US$164.99. However, buyers should check their vehicle compatibility before ordering. You may need to purchase additional dash kits, wiring harnesses, steering wheel control adapters, or hire professional installation, which can add to the total cost.

Keeping your iPhone cool while charging

Wireless charging, navigation, direct sunlight, and a hot dashboard create a "perfect storm" for your iPhone. The ESR CryoBoost MagSafe car charger tackles this with a built-in cooling fan. It combines a magnetic vent or dash mount, wireless charging, and active cooling for US$29.99, making it ideal for drivers using wireless CarPlay who still want to charge their iPhone on long drives.

If you don't need charging, a simpler MagSafe mount is available

Not every drive requires wireless charging. The standard ESR MagSafe car mount holds your iPhone on the dashboard or air vent without any extra charging cables.

This mount sells for US$15.99 and comes with a metal magnetic ring for use with phones or cases that don't support magnetic attachment. In hotter climates, this non-charging mount is actually a better fit, since charging generates extra heat.

Replacing low-quality CarPlay cables

Many CarPlay issues stem from worn or poorly connecting cables. The Anker Nano USB-A to USB-C CarPlay cable features a braided design for stable data transfer with newer USB-C iPhones, priced at US$11.99.

Drivers using an iPhone 14 or older can opt for the Anker PowerLine Flow USB-A to Lightning cable at US$17.99.

Adding fast charging for the best experience

The USB ports used for wired CarPlay in cars usually charge slowly. The Anker 323 car charger plugs into the 12V power socket and provides one USB-C port and one USB-A port.

This charger sells for US$14.99 and can charge your passengers' phones or power other accessories without interfering with the car's CarPlay connection. When using wireless CarPlay, it can also speed up your own charging.

Tidying up your installation

A pack of adhesive cable clips for US$6.99 can make a portable CarPlay display or wired phone mount installation look much neater. These clips route cables along the edges of the dashboard, keeping them away from the gear stick, pedals, and cup holders.

You don't need to buy a new car or go through a major audio upgrade to enjoy CarPlay. Depending on what your vehicle already has, everything from a better cable at US$12 to a complete portable display for around US$90 can make a big difference to everyday convenience.

Want to get even more out of CarPlay? Check out 9to5Mac's regularly updated list of over 120 CarPlay-compatible iPhone apps.
